receipt.public_excerpt: self-report cannot count as evidence of consciousness

evidence_items.explanation: The October study reports that two model families changed their claims about experience when instructions and training conditions changed, without establishing subjective experience. This supports the narrow inference that such reports alone do not establish felt pain; it does not establish that pain is absent.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Valen Tagliabue, Leonard Dung and Cameron Berg
evidence_items.locator: Section 6, Limitations and future directions, opening sentence
evidence_items.explanation: The authors report internal pain-related representations with behavioral effects, which limits any dismissal of all such states as meaningless. They also explicitly state that they have not shown conscious experience; this earlier-period study does not contradict the narrow claim about what an utterance establishes.

unresolved_gaps: The decisive experiment covers two relatively small model families and broader experience questions, not every LLM or a dedicated validation of pain reports.
Neither cited study independently measures felt pain.
The stronger contextual claim that LLMs have no experience is not settled by these findings.
